pairs.question: Nonne dicimus 'consulum officium, senatus officium, imperatoris officium'?
pairs.derivation: Cicero poses a nonne-question (expecting assent) about whether 'officium' applies to public life and answers it himself. Question is the single nonne interrogative sentence. Answer is the immediately following operative reply 'praeclare convenit'; stopped at the first full stop, cutting the subsequent challenge 'aut da melius' which turns from answering to provoking.

pairs.question: Quid igitur festinamus?
pairs.answer: Illi enim mea opera ante Kal. Ian. nihil opus est, nos autem eius voluntatem ante Idus Decembr. perspiciemus in Casca.
pairs.derivation: Direct speech: Cicero (to Oppius) asks 'quid igitur festinamus?' and answers his own question in the same quoted utterance. Dropped the speech tag 'inquam' as framing. Answer is the contiguous explanatory sentence giving the reason there is no hurry; stopped at 'perspiciemus in Casca.' before 'valde mihi adsensus est', which is narration of Oppius' reaction, not part of the answer.
